name: Ruhollah Khomeini
role: Founder and first Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran (1979-1989)
summary: Khomeini was a Shi'i jurist who argued that qualified Islamic jurists must rule and who led the 1979 revolution that replaced the Iranian monarchy with an Islamic republic under his own guardianship. He insisted that all law come from God, rejected Western liberal democracy, communism and capitalism alike ('neither East nor West'), and favoured state ownership of major industry, Islamic social morality enforced by law, and Muslim unity against the superpowers and Israel. His rule saw the suppression of opposition, the 1988 prison executions and the 1989 fatwa against Salman Rushdie.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The constitution he oversaw and urged voters to approve lists medical treatment among the basic necessities the state must provide (Art. 43) and commits public revenue to health care under social security (Art. 29); in 1979 he also promised free services.

public-ownership.rationale: Article 44 of the 1979 constitution, adopted under his leadership, puts large-scale industry, foreign trade, major minerals, banking, insurance, power generation, railroads, dams and broadcasting in public ownership run by the state.

cut-welfare.rationale: The constitution he backed obliges the state to provide social security for retirement, unemployment, disability and orphans (Art. 29), and he presented Islam as standing on the side of the weak, peasants and needy; he never argued that welfare breeds dependency.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He backed a ban on alcohol and drugs, defending flogging for drinking and saying selling heroin must be prohibited, and his government banned them after the revolution.

strong-leader.rationale: As Leader he held supreme command, final say over policy and over appointments to the Guardian Council and judiciary (Art. 110), and in 1988 ruled that the Islamic government's authority takes precedence even over secondary religious rules such as prayer and fasting when state interest requires.

state-harmful.rationale: The central argument of Islamic Government is that a state with executive power is necessary to apply Islamic law, defend the borders and collect taxes, and that without one a system of law is 'clearly deficient'.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: In Islam and Revolution he defends Islam's penal provisions against fornication (a hundred lashes, stoning for the married) as protecting nations from corruption; prostitution is not named, so this is medium.

reviewHistory.rationale: In 1979 he endorsed corporal and capital punishment for prostitution, and revolutionary courts executed prostitutes on the charge of corruption on earth.

rehabilitation.rationale: He championed Islamic punishments such as flogging, retaliation and execution, and said the penal code must not be suspended; the constitution, however, also lists reforming criminals among the judiciary's tasks (Art. 156).

traditional-family.rationale: The constitution's Article 10 calls the family the fundamental unit of Islamic society and orders all laws to protect its sanctity; he urged early marriage and the husband's headship.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Revolutionary Courts executed men for sodomy from the first months after the revolution, so the state he led treated same-sex relations as a capital matter and could not have recognised same-sex marriage.

reviewHistory.rationale: He held homosexual acts to be a capital offence and had the death penalty imposed, so same-sex marriage had no place in the law of the state he led.

abortion-legal.rationale: His rulings say a woman who becomes pregnant by adultery must not have an abortion, and Islamic law as he applied it did not permit abortion except in narrow cases.

more-religion-public.rationale: He taught that religion cannot be separated from politics and founded a state in which Islam governs law, education, media and dress.

gradual-change.rationale: He led a revolution to replace the monarchy rather than reform it, though on introducing Islamic law he said Iran would proceed in stages.

free-trade.rationale: His rulings forbid commercial relations that expose the bazaar to harm or subject Muslims to economic slavery, and he stressed self-sufficiency over reliance on foreign trade.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He said that even if humanity reaches the moon or Mars, without Islamic moral and spiritual foundations it will remain deprived of true happiness and unable to solve its social problems, though he did not oppose science and atomic industry.

revolution-justified.rationale: He led the 1978-79 revolution that overthrew the Shah, taught that Muslims must overthrow tyrannical governments, and said it is the duty of all Muslims to create a victorious Islamic revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: He argued that Islamic jurists, as experts in divine law, should govern, and the constitution gives a Guardian Council of jurists veto over legislation and over election candidates; he also urged the public to follow his recommendations at the polls.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His legal rulings say that commercial dealings with foreigners must be broken off where they risk damaging the Muslims' bazaar or reducing the country to commercial and economic slavery, and he stressed national self-sufficiency in agriculture and industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The constitution he approved bases the economy on systematic state planning and reserves the 'mother industries' for the state sector (Art. 44), so the state directs strategic industry.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He wrote that Islam has no hereditary monarchy, that monarchy and hereditary succession have no place in it, and that the Islamic government has no palaces or royal courts; he led the overthrow of the Pahlavi monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: He said Islamic government is not democratic in the Western sense because laws come from God, not from the majority's will, contrasted it with republics where majorities enact anything as law, and in 1979 rejected labels such as 'democratic republic' and threatened those acting 'in the name of democracy'.

right-to-secede.rationale: Article 9 of the constitution he oversaw makes territorial integrity inseparable and bars any authority from infringing it, even under the pretext of freedom.

reviewHistory.rationale: He refused even the Kurdish demand for autonomy in 1979 as dividing the Iranian nation and declared jihad on Kurdish rebels; no source records him addressing secession by name.

natural-rulers.rationale: He argued that the ruler must surpass others in knowledge of Islamic law and in justice, so that only qualified jurists are fit to rule, though he based this on learning and piety rather than birth.

political-violence-never.rationale: In his 1970 lectures Islamic Government he says that when a ruling group departs from Islam it will be the duty of Muslims to wage armed jihad against it.

reviewHistory.rationale: He supported armed revolution, jihad, executions of opponents and the Rushdie fatwa, and endorsed the 1981 shooting of demonstrators, so he did not regard political violence as never justified.

separate-church-state.rationale: He called the slogan separating religion from politics a colonial invention and set up a state under the guardianship of the jurist.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He held that all law must come from the Qur'an and Sunna, and Article 4 of the constitution requires all laws to be based on Islamic criteria.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He held that judging, defence and enforcement of law are state functions entrusted to Islamic rulers and judges appointed by them, and that Muslims should not take disputes to non-Islamic authorities; he gave no role to private providers.

military-superiority.rationale: Article 151 obliges the government to provide military training and equipment on the Qur'anic command to prepare all possible force to strike fear into the enemy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He said the community of Muslims is one nation without territorial or ethnic distinction, saying there is no difference between Kurds, Lurs, Turks, Persians and Baluchis, and rejected ethnic nationalism as a plot to disunite Muslims.

civilizational-union.rationale: Article 11 of the constitution says all Muslims form a single nation and obliges the state to work toward their unity; he wrote that if Muslims united in a single front the imperialists could not penetrate their lands.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He told Muslims that defending Islamic lands and enjoining good and forbidding evil are duties binding every person, which the constitution makes a reciprocal duty of all (Art. 8), and he called on people to give their lives for Islam.

restore-past-order.rationale: He held that Islamic government should return to the model of the Prophet and Imam Ali, arguing that without later corruption there would be no monarchy, empire or vice, and he called Westernising modernisation a plot.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The only evidence was a quotation from his 1988 acceptance of the ceasefire found through Wikipedia; the original was not opened, so no position is recorded here.

reviewHistory.rationale: Defending the Iran-Iraq war, he wrote 'we do not repent, nor are we sorry for even a single moment' because Iran fought to fulfil its religious duty and 'the result is a marginal issue'.

taxation-theft.rationale: He wrote that an Islamic state is financed by khums, zakat, jizya and kharaj, and that these taxes are necessary to sustain government; he called for their levying.

harm-principle.rationale: He held the state must enforce Islamic morality against alcohol, music, immodest dress and sexual vice; Article 8 of the constitution makes enjoining good and forbidding evil a duty of people and government alike.

conscription.rationale: He called defence of Islamic lands a personal duty of all Muslims, and the constitution obliges the state to give military training to all citizens (Art. 151); the war effort relied on mass mobilisation.

total-state.rationale: He held that Islam has laws for every area of life, including taxes, government and culture, and the constitution sets the state to direct education, culture and the media toward Islamic goals; in 1980 he launched the Cultural Revolution to Islamize the universities.

national-rebirth.rationale: He presented the revolution as the end of a long period of foreign plunder and moral corruption and a return to true Islam, with the Shah's decadent order to be purged.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He called Israel a 'cancerous growth' that must be fought, called for the liberation of Palestine as an Islamic land and forbade commercial and political relations with Israel, calling merchants who trade with it traitors to Islam.

national-self-determination.rationale: The constitution he oversaw calls independence and freedom the right of all peoples (Art. 154), though he refused autonomy claims by Kurds inside Iran.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He grounded politics and morals in revelation and faith in God, saying that a society without true faith cannot solve its problems.

dominated-front.rationale: He urged Muslim and other oppressed nations to unite in a single front against the superpowers, and the constitution commits Iran to support the struggles of the oppressed against the oppressors everywhere (Art. 154).

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The constitution he oversaw stresses women's role as mothers and rearers of committed human beings, and his rulings and laws gave husbands and wives different rights and duties.

ban-interest.rationale: He wrote that Islam 'radically prohibited' usury and banking on the basis of usury, called for interest-free Islamic bank loans to peasants, and the constitution he oversaw makes interest-free lending a pillar of the economy and orders confiscation of wealth gained through usury (Arts. 43, 49).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He praised an Islamic government 'that knows no difference of race, whether between black and white', and the constitution says race, colour and language confer no privilege (Art. 19).

national-mission.rationale: The constitution's preamble gives the army and Guards the mission of extending the sovereignty of God's law worldwide, and he called for exporting the Islamic revolution and establishing Islamic government worldwide.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He held that the state must run every area of life, from taxes and justice to education and culture, and the constitution assigns it wide economic and moral duties (Arts. 3, 43, 44).

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He said all Muslims are brothers regardless of race and that nobility lies only in fear of God, and Article 19 of the constitution denies privilege by race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He held that people are equal in dignity before God by piety and that race confers no privilege, but the law he approved treats religions and sexes unequally and recognises only some minorities.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: He described Israel as a creation of imperialism that expelled Muslims from their homelands and as the servant of the superpowers.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The constitution he oversaw applies Islamic law to Muslims and lets recognised minorities follow their own canons in personal status (Arts. 12-13), rather than one civil code for all.

restrict-conversion.rationale: He treated leaving Islam as apostasy, said the missionary centres of churches, Zionists and Baha'is should be destroyed, and his government rewarded conversion to Islam while persecuting Baha'is.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: His government made Islamic education central to schools and universities, Islamised the curriculum in the Cultural Revolution, and said the education system must be Islamic.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He rested the jurist's authority on divine appointment and qualifications of knowledge and justice rather than on consent, although he sought referendums (98 percent for the Islamic Republic in 1979, the constitution that December) and Art. 6 requires public opinion expressed through elections.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He called for jihad, armed struggle against rulers who violate Islam, and issued the Rushdie fatwa, so he did not hold that force may never be initiated.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Article 26 permits parties only if they do not violate the basis of the Islamic Republic, and under him parties such as the National Democratic Front and the Tudeh were outlawed for opposing the new order.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He told followers to assure the poor that Islam stands with the weak, peasants and needy, built his movement on the 'mostazafin' (oppressed), and the constitution commits the state to uproot poverty and to give housing priority to those in greatest need (Arts. 31, 43).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Under his rule Revolutionary Courts tried opponents with minimal due process, and in 1988 death commissions secretly killed thousands of prisoners outside ordinary legal process.

reviewHistory.rationale: He authorised revolutionary courts and summary trials of his opponents, ordered executions of Kurdish rebels and, in 1988, a secret order for commissions to retry and execute imprisoned dissidents, bypassing ordinary legal protections.

party-controls-media.rationale: Radio and television are state sector under the constitution he oversaw, with the Leader appointing their head (Arts. 44, 110); he banned music other than martial or religious from broadcasting in 1979 and closed opposition newspapers.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Under the constitution he led, the Leader (head of state) commands the armed forces, declares war and peace, and appoints top commanders (Art. 110); in 1979 he also named his own prime minister, Mehdi Bazargan, and demanded obedience to him.

clerical-rule.rationale: His 1970 lectures 'Islamic Government' argued that the qualified jurist must rule, and as Supreme Leader he held the highest authority under the constitution's guardianship of the jurist (Arts. 5, 107-110), with clerics controlling the Guardian Council and judiciary.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: His government banned all broadcast music except martial or religious in July 1979, banned most Western films, and his Rushdie fatwa answered a novel; he condemned theatres, cinemas, dancing and music as hotbeds of immorality.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He held Islam to be the only true and complete path and Western civilisation a corrupting imperialist culture, saying Muslims should stay independent of both East and West.

death-penalty.rationale: The Islamic Republic under him killed thousands of imprisoned dissidents in 1988 and executed men for sodomy after 1979, so capital punishment was a central tool of his rule.

reviewHistory.rationale: He upheld execution under Islamic law, ordered mass executions of opponents and in 1988 ordered the execution of imprisoned dissidents judged apostates or waging war on God.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

restrict-pornography.rationale: His government banned most Western films, mixed bathing and un-Islamic entertainment, and the constitution tasks the state with fighting vice and corruption (Art. 3).

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The constitution he oversaw makes enforcing public morality a reciprocal duty of everyone, including pressure by people on one another (Art. 8), and his government enforced conformity in dress, music and entertainment.

constituent-assembly.rationale: In January 1979 he announced a government that would convene a constituent assembly of elected representatives to approve the constitution; the draft was reworked by an elected Assembly of Experts and approved by referendum in December 1979.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The only evidence was a second-hand report of an unpublished fatwa found through Wikipedia; no original was found, so no position is recorded here.

reviewHistory.rationale: A second-hand report by the Guards commander says he rejected a 1980s proposal to start nuclear and chemical weapons work by a fatwa that was never published in detail.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The constitution he oversaw respects legitimately acquired private property but limits it: the private sector only supplements the state and cooperative sectors (Art. 44), wealth gained illicitly is confiscated (Art. 49), and public wealth is at the government's disposal in the public interest (Art. 45).

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He opposed state control of religious schools, endowments and clergy under the Shah and ruled that clerics must not accept state posts there, and he set up clerical control of the state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Article 143 of the constitution he oversaw makes the army responsible for guarding the country's territorial integrity; it does not name secession.

reviewHistory.rationale: In August 1979 he issued a fatwa declaring jihad against Kurdish rebel groups, labelled them waging war against God, and ordered army and Revolutionary Guard operations to put down the Kurdish revolt.

refugee-return.rationale: He denounced Israel for the Muslims it 'has driven from their homelands' and called on Muslims to liberate Palestine.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He condemned race and nationalism as ideas promoted to divide Muslims and called for unity based on Islam alone.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He denounced colonial rule as plunder that kept Muslim lands backward and as a plan to destroy Islam, and demanded an end to all forms of foreign control.

elective-rulers.rationale: The republic he founded fills the presidency, parliament and, through an elected Assembly of Experts, the Leadership by election and not inheritance, and he praised the 1979 referendum on ending the monarchy; the electorate is limited by Islamic criteria and clerical vetting.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He held the Shah's government illegitimate and tyrannical for violating the constitution and Islamic law, and his rulings say Muslims must denounce such rulers' wrongs publicly even when it has no practical effect and must not submit to oppression.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The parliament he approved is elected but subordinate: God alone legislates, the Guardian Council can veto any bill for incompatibility with Islam (Arts. 4, 94), and the Leader stands above it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He argued that the imperialist powers keep Muslim countries backward and dependent so as to take their oil, minerals and land and turn them into markets for foreign goods; he framed this in religious and political rather than economic-theory terms.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He said Iran, with its oil and minerals, need not beg aid or loans from America or Britain, called loans enslavement, and after the revolution celebrated self-sufficiency in food and in education; the constitution makes self-sufficiency a goal (Arts. 30, 43).

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He rejected Western political forms, writing that Islamic government is not constitutional in the Western sense nor a republic of majority-made law, and argued for Islamic institutions suited to Muslim societies.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The constitution makes the Islamic Revolutionary Guards guardians of the Revolution and an Islamic army committed to its ideology (Arts. 143-150).

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: His rulings forbid foreign political, economic or commercial influence over Muslim lands and the constitution bans any agreement giving foreigners control over the economy or resources (Art. 153) and any foreign concessions for companies in commerce, industry, agriculture or mining (Art. 81).

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Article 52 of the constitution he approved requires the government's annual budget to be submitted to the elected Islamic Consultative Assembly for approval.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He denounced turning Iran into a market for expensive unnecessary foreign goods, and after the revolution answered complaints about prices by saying he doubted the sacrifices were made for cheaper melons; the constitution's preamble hails freeing women from serving consumerism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about financial and political support, and the statement now asks only about arming insurgents.

reviewHistory.rationale: His government supplied financial and political support to allied Shia groups abroad such as Lebanese Hezbollah and the Iraqi Da'wa Party, and he called for exporting the revolution.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about financial and political support, and the statement now asks only about arming insurgents.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: He called for destroying foreign missionary and propaganda centres in Tehran, and the constitution bans any agreement giving foreigners control over the country's culture or economy (Art. 153).

job-guarantee.rationale: The constitution commits the state to full employment and to supplying means of work, but expressly through cooperatives and interest-free loans, and not by making the government a major absolute employer (Art. 43), so it stops short of an employer of last resort.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He said Baha'is were not a sect but a political party and spies backed first by Britain then by the United States, and that Jews from Islam's beginning mounted anti-Islamic propaganda.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: His rulings regulate marriage in detail as a legal and religious institution carrying rights over dowry, maintenance and inheritance.

religious-nation.rationale: He defined the community by Islam and not by territory, ethnicity or race, and the constitution declares all Muslims one nation (Art. 11) with Islam the state religion.

defeat-communism.rationale: He said Iran was 'at war with international communism no less than' with the Western powers and called the communist danger no less than America's; he also banned the Tudeh party. His 1989 letter to Gorbachev, however, was a peaceful invitation to Islam.

religion-illusion.rationale: He held that religion is the source of true happiness and that social problems cannot be solved without Islam, rejecting Marxism for denying spirituality.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He rejected both blocs ('neither Eastern nor Western'), declared a war on international communism no less than on the Western plunderers, and in his 1989 letter to Gorbachev warned against falling 'into the arms of Western capitalism' while calling Marxism a spent materialist ideology; Islam was his third course.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Revolutionary Courts under his rule executed men for sodomy from 1979 with minimal due process, and the report counts executions on this charge through the 1980s.

reviewHistory.rationale: Within weeks of taking power he imposed capital punishment for homosexual acts, and he likened executing homosexuals, prostitutes and adulterers to cutting off decayed skin.

reviewHistory.rationale: Once in power he closed newspapers, banned the National Democratic Front, the Muslim People's Republican Party and the Tudeh party, ordered security forces to shoot demonstrators in 1981, and said that democratic opponents 'must be hanged'.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: In February 1989 he issued a fatwa sentencing Salman Rushdie and those who published The Satanic Verses to death for blasphemy, and the constitution he oversaw limits worship to recognised religions (Art. 13).

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He condemned imperialist powers for seizing Muslim lands, oil and minerals for their own benefit and said the goal of the revolution was the complete elimination of imperialism.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: His legal rulings state that if an enemy attacks Muslim lands or borders, defence by any means, including sacrificing life and wealth, is a duty of every Muslim.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: His legal rulings say that rulers who allow foreign control forfeit their posts and must be punished by any means, and he wrote that Muslims have no alternative to armed holy war against governments that do not conform to Islamic law; he led the revolution against the Shah on that basis.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He held that Western culture, with its permissiveness and imperialist influence, conflicts with Islam, and that Iranians must keep Islam free of borrowings from East or West.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He held that sovereignty and the right to legislate belong to God alone; Articles 2 and 56 of the constitution he oversaw state that absolute sovereignty belongs to God and that the jurist's guardianship continues the Imams' authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: He ordered that women wear the hijab in Islamic ministries, so religious dress was required, not banned, in state institutions.

reviewHistory.rationale: Women in government institutions were required to wear Islamic dress under his rule, and clerics held state offices in religious dress.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: His rulings call for defending Muslim lands by any means, and the constitution makes an Islamic army and the Guards permanent (Arts. 143-151).

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: His slogan was 'neither East nor West', and Article 152 commits Iran to non-alignment with the hegemonist superpowers.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He rejected hereditary succession as alien to Islam, and under the constitution he oversaw the Leader is chosen by an elected Assembly of Experts from qualified jurists rather than inheriting office.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: He described Islamic government as 'government of law', with rulers bound by a fixed body of Islamic law; his own practice, such as the secret 1988 order, did not follow that.

racial-franchise.rationale: The state he founded bases political rights on Islam and citizenship, not race, and he said it knows no difference between Turk, Persian, Kurd and Baluch.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: His rulings state that a Muslim woman may not marry a non-Muslim man, and that a Muslim man may not marry a non-Muslim woman in a continuing marriage.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He wrote that no one may say that Islam's taxes and penal code are obsolete or should be suspended, and that anyone who claims so is straying from Islam.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He called nonreligious power atheistic and the tool of Satan to be fought, and his state suppressed communist and secular groups.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about prisons or punishment, and the statement now asks only whether the police should be abolished.

reviewHistory.rationale: He wrote that the ruler's duty is to punish aggressors and enforce the Islamic penal code, with qisas and hudud penalties, and his government built revolutionary courts and the Guards.

reviewHistory.rationale: His rulings state that a wife may not leave the house without her husband's permission and must submit to his sexual wishes in exchange for maintenance, and that a husband may not be compelled to serve.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Article 146 of the constitution he oversaw forbids any foreign military base in Iran, even for peaceful purposes, and he condemned the Shah's bases and capitulation agreements for American forces.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: His legal ruling says that a person who cannot prevent a wrongful killing except by killing the wrongdoer may, indeed must, kill him, and that all Muslims must defend their lands by any means including sacrificing their lives.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: He credited Islam with liberating Iran from 'the shame of Zoroastrianism' and denounced the Shah's celebrations of ancient monarchy, rejecting an unbroken line from pre-Islamic Iran.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: His speeches commemorate 'the Martyrs of Tehran' and 'the Martyrs at Qum' killed by the Shah's forces and call on Iranians to honour those fallen on God's path.

reviewHistory.rationale: He promoted martyrdom as the highest honour, promising that those who died in the Iran-Iraq war would go to paradise, and said martyrdom matters more than material prosperity.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: He taught that worship and politics are joined, called nonreligious power 'the tool of Satan' to be fought, named America the Great Satan, and treated disobedience to his Islamic government as revolt against God.

person-over-state.rationale: He called on citizens to give up their lives for Islam and for the war effort, promised martyrs paradise, and subordinated individuals to Islamic law and the Islamic community's interest.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He insisted that material progress cannot give humanity true happiness or solve social problems without a spiritual foundation; in his 1989 letter he called Marxism a materialistic ideology unable to meet humanity's real needs and said the Soviet problem was absence of faith in God.

racial-group-interests.rationale: He rejected the language of race and nationalism as a tool for dividing Muslims and said Kurds, Turks, Lurs and Persians are brothers.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: After Iran regained its lost territory in 1982 he rejected a truce and pressed the war into Iraq to topple Saddam Hussein, and the constitution's preamble gives the forces a mission of jihad for God's law beyond defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: He rejected nationality based on language or race, treating Muslims as one nation and calling nationalist divisions a colonial plot.

free-public-college.rationale: Article 3 of the constitution he oversaw sets the state the goal of free education at all levels and Art. 30 requires free secondary schooling and free higher education to the extent the country needs.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: He ruled that defending Muslim lands is every Muslim's duty and called volunteers to the Iran-Iraq war, while urging soldiers to refuse the Shah's orders to fire on protesters.

smash-state-machine.rationale: After the revolution he appointed his own government, replaced the old military and police, set up revolutionary courts and Guards, and said all remnants of the old regime must be purged; he did not simply take over the existing apparatus.

public-service-media.rationale: Broadcasting under his rule was a state monopoly with the Leader appointing its head, and the constitution requires media freedom only within Islamic criteria (Arts. 44, 110, 175); independence from government was not a goal.

religions-one-truth.rationale: He held that Islam is the only complete and true religion with a distinct, self-sufficient school of thought, and demanded that Muslims shun syncretic ideologies.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The constitution he oversaw makes the Twelver Ja'fari school the official religion, 'eternally immutable', with other schools only respected (Art. 12).

premarital-sex.rationale: His rulings and the penal system he approved treat sex outside marriage as a serious offence, and revolutionary courts punished adultery with flogging and death.

women-suffrage.rationale: Although he protested the Shah's enfranchisement of women in 1963, in 1979 he told women they must share in deciding the country's fate and urged them to vote; women sat in parliament, though the constitution reserves the Leadership for a jurist.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: He said Islam raised women's dignity, made women equal to men and has particular regard for them, thanked them for their role in the revolution, and rejected the charge of religious oppression.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: He held the Qur'an to be God's word and the source of all law, but he also delivered mystical lectures on its opening chapter treating names and verses as signs with layers of meaning, so literal reading was not his only mode.

national-church-status.rationale: The constitution makes Twelver Shi'i Islam the official state religion, with legal precedence over other religions and schools (Art. 12).

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: In his lectures he called the death penalty for heroin trading out of proportion to the offence, so he did not endorse killing drug suspects by the state without trial.

self-ownership.rationale: The law he enforced restricts people's use of their bodies, including alcohol, drugs, dress, sexual relations and suicide-related sins, so he did not hold full bodily self-ownership.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: He said he had nothing against going to the moon or building atomic installations, provided Muslims keep to Islamic values and mission, and wanted universities independent of West and East.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: He revoked the 1967 Family Protection Law, and in 1979 said women could obtain divorce only through a clause in the marriage contract or a mujtahid's decision when a husband mistreats them, whereas men could repudiate on their own.

national-resource-control.rationale: He repeatedly denounced the plunder of Iran's oil and minerals by foreign companies and the constitution forbids any agreement giving foreigners control over natural resources (Art. 153) and makes minerals and other public wealth state property (Arts. 44-45).

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: In his rulings he calls laws contrary to Islam 'void from the standpoint of both Islam and the law', and urged Muslims never to submit to oppressive rulers; he demanded obedience to laws he judged Islamic.

multipolar-world.rationale: He rejected domination by both superpowers and wanted a united Muslim world as an independent power, though he stated no model of a multipolar order.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The constitution he backed obliges the state to provide social security for retirement, unemployment, disability and orphans (Art. 29), and he presented Islam as standing on the side of the weak, peasants and needy; he never argued that welfare breeds dependency. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

religious-offensive-war.rationale: In The Little Green Book he defines jihad as the conquest of all non-Muslim territories, to be declared once a proper Islamic government exists, with the aim of putting Qur'anic law in power across the earth.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: In Islamic Government he urges Muslims to act as Imam Husayn did, who resisted until he was killed, and to drop excuses for evading that responsibility.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: He tells Muslims that against profane governments there is no alternative to armed jihad and that resigning oneself to oppression is worse than oppression.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Article 47 of the constitution he oversaw says legitimately acquired private ownership is to be respected.

notes: Where his views changed, the later position is used: in Paris in 1978-79 he promised free elections, free parties and a limited role for clerics, but from 1979 he ruled as Leader under guardianship of the jurist and suppressed opponents. Sources s1-s3 and s16 are translated selections of his lectures, speeches and rulings; the constitution (s4) is tagged as a text, not his own act, since an Assembly of Experts drafted it. Wikipedia pages (s5-s9, s11) are cited only for reported facts of his record, and an answer that rested on Wikipedia alone was re-sourced or nulled in this pass (2026-11-12): 4 answers nulled. Themes searched this pass: dress and sexual morality, the death penalty and repression (Amnesty, Boroumand Center, RFE/RL), territorial integrity, jihad, resistance to oppression, property, in his own texts and the constitution. The Political-Divine Testament and Tahrir al-Wasilah could not be retrieved (see notFound), so their content is not used. The statements added since the first pass (candidates and others) were checked against the texts; those his sources do not settle are null.
